ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the library

3. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

4. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

5. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

7. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

8. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

9. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. goed

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

13. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. happiness

14. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word classes: verb aspect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
